published.title: The Cassels–Tate pairing on polarized abelian varieties

comparison: Corollaries4/7 and Theorem8(3) match in required mathematical scope. Published notation incorrectly equates maximal-divisible membership with individual divisibility without a hypothesis; corrected author text adds finiteness of M[p] for every prime before identifying Mdiv with intersection nM. Current main proves maximality for its actual displayed divisible-summand/finite-quotient decomposition and explicitly does not invoke the arbitrary-group identification.
application: For an elliptic curve E/Q, its canonical principal polarization has c=0 because Pic^0(E) has its rational identity. Cor7 gives alternation; nondegeneracy after quotient by maximal divisible subgroup is the pairing convention stated in the introduction. Distinct primary components are orthogonal. The finite2-primary quotient F therefore has nondegenerate alternating pairing, and paired cyclic factors make dim_F2 F[2] even. Alternatively Theorem8(3) states the needed2-torsion square condition directly. Finiteness of all Sha is not assumed. Finite-level Selmer structure, Kummer and rank calculations remain separate inputs.
limits: This is a source-version/application comparison, not a reproof of Cassels–Tate, a proof of finite Sha, or a new approval of all pole/RC ancestors.
